questions.question:
An amplifier using an opamp with a slew-rate SR = 1V/[latex]\mu[/latex] sec has a gain of 40 dB.
If this amplifier has to faithfully amplify sinusoidal signals from dc to 20 KHz
without introducing any slew-rate induced distortion, then the input signal level
must not exceed.
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Slew rate } &=A \cdot 2 \pi f V_{m} \\ V &=A V_{m} \sin \omega t \\ \frac{d V}{d t} &=A V_{m} \omega \cos \omega t \\ \left.\frac{d V}{d t}\right|_{\max } &=S R=A V_{m} 2 \pi f_{m} \\ 20 \log x &=40 \\ x &=100=A \\ \Rightarrow V_{m}=\frac{S R}{A \cdot 2 \pi f_{m}} &=\frac{1}{10^{-6} \times 100 \times 2 \pi \times 20 \times 10^{3}} \\ V_{m} &=79.5 \mathrm{mV} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Slew rate } &=A \cdot 2 \pi f V_{m} \\ V &=A V_{m} \sin \omega t \\ \frac{d V}{d t} &=A V_{m} \omega \cos \omega t \\ \left.\frac{d V}{d t}\right|_{\max } &=S R=A V_{m} 2 \pi f_{m} \\ 20 \log x &=40 \\ x &=100=A \\ \Rightarrow V_{m}=\frac{S R}{A \cdot 2 \pi f_{m}} &=\frac{1}{10^{-6} \times 100 \times 2 \pi \times 20 \times 10^{3}} \\ V_{m} &=79.5 \mathrm{mV} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: An angle modulated signal is given by [latex]s(t)=cos2\pi (2\times 10^{6}t+30 sin 150t+40 cos 150t)[/latex] The maximum frequency and phase deviations of s(t) are
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} s(t) &=\cos [2 \pi \times 2 \times 10^{6} t+2 \pi \times 30 \sin 150 t \\&+2 \pi \times 40 \cos 150 t] \\ \frac{d \phi}{d t} &=2 \pi \times 2 \times 10^{6}\\ & +2 \pi \times 4500 \cos 150 t+2 \pi \times 6000(-\sin 150 t) \\ \therefore \Delta \omega &=\omega_{1}-\omega_{c}=2 \pi\left(4500^{2}+6000^{2}\right)^{1 / 2} \\ &=2 \pi \times 7.5 \mathrm{k} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \therefore \quad \Delta f &=\frac{\Delta \omega}{2 \pi}=7.5 \mathrm{kHz} \\ \Delta \phi &=2 \pi \sqrt{30^{2}+40^{2}} \\ \Delta \phi &=100 \pi \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: In the figure, [latex]m(t)=\frac{2\sin 2\pi t}{t}[/latex], [latex]s(t)=\cos 200\pi t[/latex] and [latex] n(t)=\frac{\sin 199\pi t}{t}[/latex]. The output y(t) will be
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} m(t) \times s(t) &=\frac{2 \sin 2 \pi t}{t} \times \cos 200 \pi t \\ &=\frac{1}{t}(\sin 202 \pi t-\sin 198 \pi t) \end{aligned} [/latex] The signal at the input of the LPF will be, [latex] x(t)=[m(t) s(t)+n(t)] s(t) [/latex] [latex] =\frac{1}{t}(\sin 202 \pi t-\sin 198 \pi t+\sin 199 \pi t) \cos 200 \pi t [/latex] [latex] =\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 402 \pi t+\sin 399 \pi t-\sin 398 \pi t) [/latex] [latex] \quad+\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t+\sin 2 \pi t-\sin \pi t) [/latex] After passing [latex]\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 402 \pi t+\sin 399 \pi t-\sin 398 \pi t) [/latex]  term through LPF with cut-off frequency of 1 Hz , it results in a component of [latex]\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t)[/latex] at the output. So, after passing x(t) through the LPF, we get, [latex] \begin{aligned} y(t) &=\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t)+\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t+\sin 2 \pi t-\sin \pi t) \\ &=\frac{\sin 2 \pi t}{t}+\frac{1}{2 t}(2 \sin 0.5 \pi t \cos 1.5 \pi t) \\ y(t) &=\frac{\sin 2 \pi t}{t}+\frac{\sin 0.5 \pi t}{t} \cos 1.5 \pi t \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} m(t) \times s(t) &=\frac{2 \sin 2 \pi t}{t} \times \cos 200 \pi t \\ &=\frac{1}{t}(\sin 202 \pi t-\sin 198 \pi t) \end{aligned} [/latex]
The signal at the input of the LPF will be,
[latex] x(t)=[m(t) s(t)+n(t)] s(t) [/latex]
[latex] =\frac{1}{t}(\sin 202 \pi t-\sin 198 \pi t+\sin 199 \pi t) \cos 200 \pi t [/latex]
[latex] =\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 402 \pi t+\sin 399 \pi t-\sin 398 \pi t) [/latex]
[latex] \quad+\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t+\sin 2 \pi t-\sin \pi t) [/latex]
After passing [latex]\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 402 \pi t+\sin 399 \pi t-\sin 398 \pi t) [/latex] term through LPF with cut-off frequency of 1 Hz , it results in a component of [latex]\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t)[/latex] at the output.
So, after passing x(t) through the LPF, we get,
[latex] \begin{aligned} y(t) &=\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t)+\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t+\sin 2 \pi t-\sin \pi t) \\ &=\frac{\sin 2 \pi t}{t}+\frac{1}{2 t}(2 \sin 0.5 \pi t \cos 1.5 \pi t) \\ y(t) &=\frac{\sin 2 \pi t}{t}+\frac{\sin 0.5 \pi t}{t} \cos 1.5 \pi t \end{aligned}[/latex]
